# soapysdr-tools

**Command-line tools for the SoapySDR hardware abstraction layer**

- **Version recorded:** 0.8.1
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/pothosware/SoapySDR/wiki>

## What it does

Carries `SoapySDRUtil`, which enumerates every SDR the system can see through SoapySDR, prints its capabilities -- sample rates, gain stages, antenna ports, tuning ranges -- and runs a rate test against it. SoapySDR itself is the abstraction layer; this is how you interrogate it.

## Why you would want it

`SoapySDRUtil --find` is the first command to run when an SDR is not working, and it answers a question nothing else does cleanly: does the software layer see the device at all. It separates a USB or permissions problem from a driver problem from an application problem, which is three evenings saved.

## Before it will work

A per-device SoapySDR module for whatever hardware you have. This catalog carries them separately -- soapysdr-module-rtlsdr, -hackrf, -airspy and the rest -- because a user needs the one matching their device, not all twelve (D-020). Device access usually means a udev rule and the `plugdev` group.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install soapysdr-tools --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `soapysdr-tools`

## Known problems

An empty `--find` with the device plugged in almost always means the matching module is not installed, or that permissions stop the process opening the USB device -- and the output is the same silence in both cases. Check `lsusb` first, then whether the module package is present, then the permissions.
